subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default into delete-after-run cleanup, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain one-shot-only and invalid?
rationale: Both directions are represented by open PRs, and choosing one changes persisted cron lifecycle semantics for existing users.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require upgrade/load or doctor handling for existing omitted jobs and reconcile the strict-rejection PR.

options.title: Keep deleteAfterRun one-shot-only
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its UI and Gateway blockers are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new-job default and document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require upgrade/load or doctor handling for existing omitted jobs and reconcile the strict-rejection PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron normalization, SQLite store, and trigger/default history makes this the strongest available owner signal for the lifecycle-contract choice.
